subject.title: [Bug]: Subagents can appear completed before the underlying delegated work is actually finished

question: Should subagent completion remain tied to child agent-run terminal state while child-owned background exec/process sessions are surfaced separately, or should those process sessions block subagent task completion?
rationale: Both behaviors are plausible product contracts, and the current docs/code separate authoritative agent-run task completion from process registry liveness while the issue expects delegated background work to affect completion state.

options.title: Surface background work separately
options.body: Keep child agent-run completion authoritative, but make child-owned process sessions visible in tasks/session status and parent handoff so users are not told all delegated work is done.

options.title: Block on child process liveness
options.body: Treat scoped child-owned background process sessions as part of subagent completion with timeout, cancellation, and explicit detached-work escape rules.

options.title: Document current semantics
options.body: Clarify that subagent completion means the child agent turn ended and that background processes must be tracked through process/task status, accepting the current behavior as intentional.

recommendation.title: Surface background work separately
recommendation.body: Keep child agent-run completion authoritative, but make child-owned process sessions visible in tasks/session status and parent handoff so users are not told all delegated work is done.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent subagent lifecycle and cleanup stabilization commits make this the closest available owner for the runtime contract decision.
